# AskWise: Execution-Guided Clarification of Intent and Data in Text-to-SQL

## Research question

Queries agreeing on observed records can diverge after a data correction, making intent clarification and record checking interdependent.

## Method

AskWise maintains query–repair worlds. A question requires two executed worlds differing only in that choice with different answers; answering requires known agreement across all surviving worlds. An exact four-cell bound compares EC2 question gains under uniform binary worlds and Boolean outputs.

## Evaluation

Policy evaluation uses 120 synthetic sales tasks with 16 equally likely worlds each, truthful simulated responses and precomputed SQLite answers. Separate AmbiQT experiments audit 1,206 eligible value swaps and prune identical model candidates on 155 questions from 20 databases.

## What the results support

The exact bound requests fewer executions than a partition relaxation; immediate witnessing needs fewer still but asks slightly more questions. Comparing both database states preserves additional reference signatures. Missing candidates remain unrecoverable, and precision changes are inconclusive.

## Limits and qualifications

Correctness assumes the intended query and true data state lie in the supplied space. The exact bound excludes dependent repairs, unequal priors and unequal question costs. Reported decision timings omit live SQL execution. One AmbiQT category and controlled swaps do not estimate natural repair prevalence. Signature matching preserves duplicate rows but ignores row order and requires column order; it is not universal equivalence or human intent validation. Error annotations use one model pass, not an independent human gold audit.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Core clarification research linking intent choices to data uncertainty, with explicit finite-world and simulated-user boundaries rather than demonstrated unanswerability handling.
